correctness.rationale: On the strict \(R^kI_+L^kI_-\) itinerary cylinder the first half-return is \(M\alpha^kx-MS_k\) and the full return has multiplier \((M\alpha^k)^2\). Except when the multiplier is one, the full return has the unique symmetric fixed value \(X_k\); checking all intermediate states gives strict admissibility precisely when \(\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\alpha^{-j}<M-1\). At multiplier one, the entire open interval \(J_k=(M(S_k-1),M)\) has identity return, and no such orbit exists when admissibility fails. Exactly one positive-inner-cell visit per full itinerary proves least period \(2(k+1)\). Monotonicity of the threshold sum yields the finite cutoff \(k<M\), and for \(M=5\) exact algebra proves attraction only for \(k=1,2\) and determines the two stated parameter windows. The standalone SymPy checker passed 63 symbolic and exact algebraic-witness tests; universal conclusions follow from the proof, not enumeration. Branch boundaries and global basin assertions are excluded.
